objective: Prevent measured autonomous lexical loops without the functional regressions caused by global token n-gram bans and without adding task templates, facts, teacher material, or learned parameters.

controlling_evidence.measured_bottleneck: Five of 120 byte-target observations entered novel lexical loops; token-level 4-gram bans cleared the benchmark but damaged legitimate structured English generation.

candidate_lock.selection_rule: If and only if the current greedy token would introduce the first repeated lexical 4-gram not present in the prompt, reject that token and select the next highest logit. Normal punctuation, formatting, lexical sequences copied from the prompt, and nonrepeating language remain eligible.

decision_rule: Implement and screen exactly one lexical-guard threshold. Reject rather than sweep thresholds or add prompt-family handlers if either the complete validation suite or repeated CPU benchmark fails.
claim_boundary: This is a generic deterministic decoding guard against measured lexical collapse. It does not add English knowledge, prove teacher equivalence, or repair any prompt family symbolically.
